title: Value-in-use: chips for ESCP's learning device (mock exam 2023/24 & 2025/26)
text: ESCP introduces a new online learning device and needs 400 chips for it. ESCP pays 6 € per chip, and the chips need to be changed twice per year. By selling these chips, the supplier has a margin of 3 € per chip.
A new chip technology is introduced that has twice the endurance. The supplier's margin for the new chips is 8 € per chip. The supplier wants to determine the value-in-use (VIU) of the new chips.
Add-on: the new technology also allows a longer time between maintenance – 12 months instead of 6 months – and the cost of each shutdown is 1,000 €.

title: Value-in-use: Z-rings vs Y-rings (exam 2019/20)
text: You are the CEO of a car manufacturer. One production line uses 250 Z-rings to connect it with the power distribution centre. Your buying department pays 8 € per Z-ring, and the rings must be changed during regular maintenance every three months.
A new product (Y-rings) has been developed that has twice the lifespan of the Z-rings. Add-on: each shutdown of the production line costs 3,000 €.

title: Startup OMG: comparing two website versions
text: The startup OMG sells trendy sneakers and wants to know which website version performs better – the early version A or the new version B. Data from a social media platform:
Use: click-through rate = clicks / visitors; conversion rate = sales / visitors; (ad) cost per sale = ad spend / sales; return on ad investment = (revenue − ad spend) / ad spend.
